newsitem.title: GERMANY: THIRD DIKE BURSTS IN FLOOD-HIT EASTERN GERMANY.
newsitem.headline: THIRD DIKE BURSTS IN FLOOD-HIT EASTERN GERMANY.

text.p: A third dike reinforcing the Oder river between Germany and Poland burst early on Sunday, flooding a German village and forcing the evacuation of 67 people, local officials said on Sunday.

They said emergency teams of soldiers, border guards and volunteers were working round the clock to shore up other flood barriers along the river and would decide whether to repair the newest breach, now one km (half a mile) in width.
The latest dike to crumble was near another which broke up last week near the village of Brieskow-Finkenheerd just south of Frankfurt an der Oder.

Flooding this month, the worst in the region in centuries, has claimed more than 100 lives in neighbouring Poland and the Czech Republic. The raging waters have eroded barriers on the German side of the Oder, which is known as the Odra in the other two countries, and threatened to inundate Germany's fertile Oderbruch plains north of Frankfurt an der Oder.
Local officials said water levels had risen south and north of the city and they warned that the flooding of the plains could force up to 19,000 Germans from their homes.
Thousands of German soldiers have been toiling around the clock to shore up flood barriers on the river.
Officials said the situation in Ratzdorf upstream at the confluence of the Oder and Neisse rivers was stable.

Germany so far has escaped the worst of the flooding, but some towns have suffered power cuts and overflowing sewage systems. Hundreds of Germans have been ordered to leave parts of the danger zone this week, and farmers have started moving out thousands of head of livestock to higher ground.
